title: Sunny and the Baby Wombat | Bedtime Story
description: Sunny the Quokka discovers a baby wombat who has wandered just a little way from its burrow and is sitting in the moonlight looking sturdy and serious and absolutely perfect. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories.
narration:
There was a small wombat on the path.

Sunny came around the bend and nearly tripped over it. The wombat — very young, judging by its size — sat in the middle of the path and looked at her with dark, serious eyes. Round and low and compact, its fur the colour of dry earth.

It did not move.

Neither did she.

The baby wombat regarded her in a way that suggested it had seen everything before and found it all unsurprising. It blinked once — slow and deliberate — and went back to whatever it had been doing, which appeared to be sitting and existing very firmly in its own small body.

Sunny smiled.

She sat down on the path a few steps away.

The wombat sniffed the air in her direction, then determined she was not food and went back to its serious sitting.

Its little nose twitched. Its ears were round and small. It was perhaps the solidest thing she had ever seen — four short legs planted wide, chest forward, as if ready to anchor itself to the earth if anyone tried to move it.

She thought: it knows exactly who it is.

The wombat turned slowly and waddled back toward the darkness — toward its burrow, she supposed. Unhurried. Certain.

She watched it go.

She sat on the path for a long time after, feeling certain too.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, baby wombat. Goodnight, little one.
